options.text: The study of weather patterns
The study of rocks and minerals
The study of how living organisms interact with each other and their environment
The study of human diseases

questions.explanation: Ecology is the study of the relationships between living organisms and their environment. It examines how organisms interact with each other and with their physical surroundings, and how energy and matter flow through ecosystems.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a community and an ecosystem?

options.text: An ecosystem is smaller than a community
A community includes only plants; an ecosystem includes animals
They are the same thing
A community is all the populations in an area; an ecosystem also includes the physical environment

questions.explanation: A community consists of all the populations of all different species living in an area. An ecosystem includes the community plus its physical (abiotic) environment, such as temperature, light, water, and soil.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an abiotic factor?

options.text: Temperature
Predation
Competition
Disease

questions.explanation: Temperature is an abiotic (non-living) factor. Abiotic factors include temperature, light, water, pH, and mineral content. Predation, competition, and disease are biotic (living) factors.

options.text: The role an organism plays in its ecosystem
The place where an organism lives
The food an organism eats
A group of organisms of the same species

questions.explanation: A habitat is the place where an organism lives. It provides the conditions and resources that the organism needs to survive, such as food, water, shelter, and appropriate temperature.

questions.stem: What does interdependence mean in ecology?

options.text: Organisms can survive without any other species
Plants depend on animals but not the other way around
Organisms in a community depend on each other for survival
Only predators depend on prey

questions.explanation: Interdependence means that organisms in a community rely on each other for survival. For example, plants provide food and oxygen for animals, while animals help pollinate plants and recycle nutrients through decomposition.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a biotic factor?

options.text: Competition between organisms
Soil pH
Wind speed
Light intensity

questions.explanation: Competition between organisms is a biotic (living) factor. Biotic factors involve the influence of other living organisms, including predation, disease, food availability, and competition for resources.

questions.stem: What is a population in ecology?

options.text: All the ecosystems on Earth
All organisms living in an area
All organisms of one species living in an area at the same time
All the plants in an area

questions.explanation: A population is all the organisms of one species living in a particular area at the same time. For example, all the rabbits in a field form a population. All populations together form a community.
